about: Share of local government direct expenditure (current operations + construction/land/equipment + interest, 2022 fiscal year) by game spending function, split across the five types of local government. Computed from the Census Bureau 2022 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances state-by-type estimates file (22statetypepu.txt), cross-checked against the Individual Unit File (national totals match to within 0.1 percent). Census item codes were mapped to game functions: schools = E12/F12/E21/F21; higherEducation = E16/F16/E18/F18; welfareAndMedicaid = E77/F77/E79/F79/E85/F85; healthAndHospitals = E32/F32/E36/F36; highways = E44/F44/E45/F45; police = E62/F62; fire = E24/F24; corrections = E04/F04/E05/F05; parks = E61/F61; housing = E50/F50; naturalResources = E59/F59; administration = E23/F23 (financial), E25/F25 (judicial and legal), E29/F29 (central staff), E31/F31 (public buildings); interest = I89 (general debt); otherPrograms = everything else (airports, miscellaneous commercial, libraries, parking, protective inspection, sewerage, solid waste, ports, other general NEC, liquor stores, water/electric/gas/transit utilities including their interest, scholarships, employment security). Shares are of direct expenditure only, not intergovernmental transfers (M/Q codes). Census 'city' is the game's municipal; 'independent school district' covers school districts. No number came from memory. Limits: dependent school systems (common in New England, Virginia, Maryland and elsewhere) are reported under the parent county, municipality or township, so schoolDistrict understates schools there and the state rows show it. Special-district and school-district shares in states with no such units are 0. District of Columbia is a single consolidated government counted by Census as municipal. Territories (Puerto Rico, Guam, USVI, American Samoa, Northern Marianas) are not in the Census Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances, so they have no state rows; use the national block as an estimate for them. A state omits a function when its local governments reported no spending on it (for example, higherEducation in states with no local colleges); use the national block as the fallback only if a game needs a value.

estimated.territories: Puerto Rico, Guam, USVI, American Samoa and Northern Marianas are absent from the Census file; use the national block as an estimate (source: derived from the 50-state-plus-DC totals, spread is the state-to-state variation in the states block).
